title: Cron Log Forensics
description: Analyse /var/log/cron.log: count backup failures and find the first failure's timestamp.
scenario: The backup script 'ran' all night according to cron, yet this morning's restore attempt failed. Analyse /var/log/cron.log: count how many backup.sh runs FAILED, and record the timestamp of the first failure. Write both answers to /home/intern/cron-report.txt as `failed-backups=<n>` and `first-failure=<timestamp>`.
symptoms: The nightly restore failed even though cron shows the job ran
/var/log/cron.log records CMD OK and CMD FAILED lines per run
Nobody knows how many runs failed or when the failures started
The incident ticket wants the answers in /home/intern/cron-report.txt
mission: Create /home/intern/cron-report.txt with `failed-backups=3` and `first-failure=Jun 16 02:15:02`, both derived from /var/log/cron.log with grep/awk.

hints.title: Filter twice
hints.content: First select the failure lines (`grep 'CMD FAILED'`), then narrow to this job (`grep backup.sh`) — combining both in one regex also works: `grep 'CMD FAILED.*backup.sh'`.

hints.title: Timestamps are the first three fields
hints.content: Syslog lines start with 'Month Day Time' — awk '{print $1, $2, $3}' extracts it: Jun 16 02:15:02.

hints.title: head -1 after sorting by time
hints.content: Log lines are chronological, so the first failure is the first matching line.
